title: With ‘Clarissa,’ Two Nigerian Brothers Are Forging an Arthouse Alternative to Nollywood
summary: Chuko and Arie Esiri's "Clarissa" is the second Nigerian film to ever play Cannes. With Neon as its global distributor, they pair tell IndieWire they hope to build a new Nigerian wave of cinema.

title: To Financiers, Films Are No Longer the Product.  Relationships with Audiences Are
summary: Decision-makers behind an eclectic group of film financing companies stopped by The American Pavilion at Cannes for a conversation about one of the most complex and ever-changing aspects of the industry.

title: Ira Sachs Cast Rami Malek to Sing in ‘The Man I Love’ Without Seeing ‘Bohemian Rhapsody’
summary: Sachs and co-writer Mauricio Zacharias tell IndieWire about the beauty and horror of gay life in 1980s NYC, and borrowing their film’s title from the 1941 Raoul Walsh classic.

title: Cannes 2026 Movies Sold So Far: Critics’ Week Winner ‘La Gradiva’ Bought by 1-2 Special
summary: The directorial debut of filmmaker Marine Atlan is a high school coming of age film that won the section's Grand Prize.

title: Billy Bob Thornton Relishes His Magic Hour Moment with Ali Larter in the ‘Landman’ Season 2 Finale
summary: "For us, it was just one of those scenes where you need to stay connected the whole time until you're done with it," said the Emmy-nominated actor of their final scene in Season 2of the Paramount+ hit.

title: Lawrence Kasdan’s Relationship with One of His Best Friends Yielded One of His Best Movies
summary: The director talks about his most recent film, the documentary "Marty, Life Is Short," and looks back at the beginning of his career as his directorial debut "Body Heat" is newly released by Criterion.

title: How a Tribe of Cinematographers Shoot ‘Survivor’ — 50 Times Over
summary: Veterans of the CBS show's camera team explain how they work behind the lens to turn a reality competition into cinematic filmmaking.

title: ‘Victorian Psycho’ Review: Maika Monroe Scares Up a Very Different Kind of Final Girl
summary: Cannes: In Zachary Wigon’s deliciously dark adaptation of Virginia Feito's novel of the same name, the beloved scream queen switches sides. Kind of.

title: ‘A Man of His Time’ Review: Swann Arlaud Plays a Fly on the Wall to Creeping Fascism
summary: Cannes: Emmanuel Marre fictionalizes the experiences of his great-grandfather in this bold political drama, who was a functionary in France’s collaborationist government during World War II.

title: ‘Roma Elastica’ Review: Marion Cotillard Is a Dying Scream Queen in Bertrand Mandico’s Film Industry Pastiche
summary: Cannes: One of cinema's most idiosyncratic auteurs delivers a kaleidoscope of riffs and references that showcase his baroquely wrought aesthetic, even if the story is thin.

title: ‘La Gradiva’ Review: Cannes Critics’ Week Winner Is a Wholly Transporting Story of Youth
summary: Cannes: Mercifully free of typical high school movie tropes, the teenagers at the heart of Marine Atlan’s film are fully realized people, allowing this stunning work to reach toward the sublime.

title: ‘The Black Ball’ Review: Los Javis’ Era-Spanning Monument to Gay Storytellers Is a Heartbreaking Work of Staggering Genius
summary: Cannes: Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi blend real and imaginary people in this Lorca-inspired ode to love stories buried by Spanish history.
